harmonicFunction: E5 (I) - Rock tonic providing huge low-end power and open string chime
C#m7 (vi7) - Minor submediant adding emotional bittersweet gravity
Aadd9 (IVadd9) - Subdominant chord with ringing open high B and E strings delivering uplifting dream-rock warmth
Bsus4 (V) - Suspended dominant chord building energy before resolving home to E

techniques.name: Melodic Octave Riffing & Open-String Chime
techniques.description: Fretting octave intervals on the 5th (A) and 3rd (G) strings while muting the middle D string with the pad of your index finger

notes: Octave shapes: E (7th fret A, 9th fret G), C# (4th fret A, 6th fret G)
Muted D string: Let your index finger lean lightly against the 4th string to silence it completely
Open string resonance: Let strings 1 and 2 ring open during chord transitions
sequence: Position index finger on fret 7 of A string, pinky on fret 9 of G string
Rest the underside of your index finger on string 4
Slide smoothly down to fret 4 (C# octave) and into open E power chords
tips: Octaves require firm fretting pressure on the active strings but zero tension in the right wrist
Dave Grohl and Pat Smear layered multiple guitars (Gibson Trini Lopez into Mesa Dual Rectifier and Vox AC30) for thickness
Lock into the slow, pounding 77 BPM groove—don't rush

beginner.title: Chorus Power Chords
steps: Learn the open power chords: E5, C#m7 (fret 4), and Aadd9
Practice steady eighth-note strumming at 77 BPM
Focus on the dynamic transition from verse to chorus

intermediate.title: Octave Riffing Technique
steps: Master the A-and-G string octave shape with index and pinky
Ensure the middle D string is completely muted with no unwanted notes
Slide smoothly between the 7th and 4th fret octaves in time with the drums

advanced.title: Dynamic Control & Stadium Energy
steps: Perform the entire song with full dynamic control from delicate verse to roaring chorus
Lock tightly with the drum roll groove without rushing the 77 BPM tempo
Replicate the layered dual-amp tone (Mesa crunch + Vox chime)

commonMistakes: Letting the middle D string ring open during octave slides
Rushing the tempo during the heavy drum intros (stay locked at 77 BPM)
Over-strumming during the verse instead of maintaining tight palm muting
practiceRoutine: 5 minutes: Octave muting drill on strings 5, 4, and 3
5 minutes: Octave slide timing at 65 BPM → 77 BPM
5 minutes: Chorus open chord dynamic strumming
metronomeWork: Practice the octave riff with metronome at 77 BPM
Focus on landing the octave slide down to fret 4 exactly on beat 1
